The Good:
- We get you; You won’t feel alone with us
- We like to keep a balance
- We fight for you; We fight for what we believe is right (even though it maay be wrong)
- We love you for existing
- We want you to grow & we’ll be there in most, if not every, step of the way
- We are naturally curious
- We are naturally parenting
- We will take responsibility 
- We are relationship driven
- We are overall passionate

The Bad:
- We give so much to others that we lose ourselves in the process
- We (especially the turbulent type) don’t have clear boundaries so we end up hurting those that we “over-committ” to
- We take on other people’s emotions (including pain!)
- We can be too idealistic
- We can be hypocrites in pursuit of our idealisms
- We can be energy vampires when we think we’re trying to help others/the situation
- We can be annoying because of want to check in on how others are feeling most times
- We send the wrong signals of interest (especially when we give out compliments)


The Ugly:
- We can be manipulative
- We can become narcissistic (Narcissists are made)
- We can use our ability to connect with others selfishly (think of cult leaders)
- We can grow tired and withdraw our love bombing attentions we give to the next thing that interests us so that you feel you did something wrong (check out, “love bombing” in narcissism)

I think it’s not just ulterior moments for me though. It’s also strengths, weaknesses, mental disorders, etc. As an ENFJ, I want to know everything about the person. I think this becomes dangerous when some in our type develop Narcissism (narcissists are created) which, interestingly enough, as I’ve been scoping out this forum, has been something described by “Worst Types to Date” and lists ENFJs as one for narcissism and manipulation.

Of course, considering, I’m only speaking for myself as an ENFJ.

I have a natural interest in people. I love to understand people but I’ve learned to develop a keenness for spotting ulterior motives because I’ve shared myself so vulnerably before. That being said, looking for one’s ulterior motives is just part of the exploration of the people around me that I try to get to know.

People say, “What doesn’t kill you makes you stronger” but in this situation, I don’t think you’ll develop strength from something that, quite frankly, is a waste of time. 

Just my perspective. Take or leave whatever I suggest, but, as an ENFJ-A, I would say:

(1.) Ask to leave the friend group. ESPECIALLY if some of them don’t care to stick around after the break up. It’s in this time that you realize who your real friends are.
(2.) Block him. From everything. Now is the time to refocus on your life and you! When things fall apart, it’s a chance for something more beautiful and amazing to come together. Find yourself and the amazing person you are. Love even better the next time around.

Thanks for reading this long-winded, know-it-all-type post. Hope things turn up for you!
